title: Refuse readings that omit a request acceptance bullet
summary: Add a reading-acceptance check that parses the request's "Acceptance:" bullets and refuses, naming the bullet, any reading whose criteria do not cover one, unless the request allows a split. Tests live in reading.rs, with a refusal-corpus case and a CHANGELOG entry. Audience: the Athena owner and the verifier, who judge readings at acceptance.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria require new unit tests, a corpus case, and cargo test, clippy -D warnings and fmt to pass.
Criteria run check_reading_acceptance on accepted and refused readings.
The outcome is a refused reading naming the missing bullet, not the existence of the check.
The rule is enforced as a step! in refusing_check.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs (check_reading_acceptance calls refusing_check, which runs step!(check_...) lines in order; the new check is added as one step! line after check_outcome_state, never as a direct call), crates/athena-core/src/reading/outcome.rs (check_outcome_state, the closest model for a request-versus-reading check), crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs (the tests module and the existing check_reading_acceptance tests) and crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs (it fails when a step! check has no corpus case in which it refuses). No record or data file is added under crates/, so check_record_file, AnyRecord and the round-trip test are not touched. Coverage is measured directly: the check compares each parsed request bullet with the reading's criteria text, and the tests call check_reading_acceptance with a real request string.

Request bullets are the '- ', '* ' or 'N.' lines under the request's 'Acceptance:' heading, up to the next blank line or 'Files:' line. A bullet is covered when a criterion contains its significant words, or a distinctive quoted or path token from it. The matching reuses existing stem and stop-list helpers where they exist.

The request 'allows a split' when its text says so, for example 'split', 'follow-up' or 'in parts' outside the Acceptance bullets. The check then does not refuse. A reading may propose a split only through the question field, never by dropping a bullet.

The refusal error names the missing bullet verbatim and says to cover it or ask a question. It is a new refusal rule, so the CHANGELOG states that it refuses more readings, that the higher refusal rate is intended, and 'expected 10% of newly refused readings' (an estimate, not measured).

The new check lives in crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs, or in a small new module under reading/, and is wired into refusing_check. The request lists only reading.rs and CHANGELOG.md, but the gate code and its mandatory corpus case sit in those other files, so they are deliverables too.

Existing readings in reading.rs tests that use a request with an Acceptance section may need criteria that cover every bullet, so those fixtures are adjusted. Consumers: none found (no config deliverable).

acceptance_criteria.text: A new test in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs calls check_reading_acceptance with a request holding two Acceptance bullets and a reading whose criteria cover only one. It asserts an Err whose text names the omitted bullet, and a second reading covering both returns Ok. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
A test shows a request that allows a split (it says so in its text) does not refuse a reading that covers fewer bullets. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.

The refusal-corpus test passes with a new case in crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs in which the new step! check is the one that refuses. Run: cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus.
The new check is one step! line in refusing_check in crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs, and the doc of check_reading_acceptance links it. Check with Grep and cargo test -p athena-core.
cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test all pass.
The change refuses more readings and the higher refusal rate is intended: expected 10% of newly refused readings (an estimate).
CHANGELOG.md has an Unreleased entry naming the new check, that it refuses more readings, that the higher refusal rate is intended, and 'expected 10% of newly refused readings'.
The doc comment of the new check names the 2026-10-29 job that was rejected for a split the reading chose, and says a split may be proposed only as a question, never by dropping a bullet.

out_of_scope: Changing reader prompts (the reader prompt set has only 2 tokens of headroom).
Auto-splitting jobs or changing the small-job default beyond forbidding dropped bullets.
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml or CI workflows.
Replaying past readings beyond the declared estimate.
departures: Higher cost and lower pass rate than the reference: this is a new refusal rule in the shared gate. It needs bullet-matching heuristics, a mandatory corpus case and fixture updates across existing tests.
urgent_reason: Cuts the wasted full job that runs before a dropped acceptance bullet is caught at the final verdict.
hard_reason: Adds a new refusal rule to the reading acceptance gate (refusing_check), which can refuse work.
